semanticText:
# Activation Clause

Establishes a document’s party roster, acceptance boundary and access guard. Activation requires the required parties’ acceptance, unchanged agreed terms and sufficient timeline access. Hosted bootstrap resolves account locators into authenticated transports before initialization; a party description alone establishes neither authority nor consent.

## Configuration

Configuration is supplied in `parameters`. The runtime uses `/activation` and `/clauses/activation/parameters` in the executing document.

- `parties` must be a nonempty dictionary. Each party requires `lead/channel`; optional `representatives` supply additional channels. Party and representative names must be nonempty and exclude `.`, `/`, `~` and `__`. Lead channels use the party key; additional channels use `party__representative`. Party `displayName`, `partyId` and `business`, and representative `displayName` and `representativeId`, describe identities without proving authority.
- `required` defaults to all initial party keys. `revision` defaults to `1`. Initialization starts with no recorded approvals.
- `accessPaths` defaults to `[]` and identifies embedded Timeline Access documents. `readers` defaults to `{}` and supplies additional groups of alternative reader keys. Party `readerKeys` and each additional representative’s `readerKeys` supply their own groups, replacing identically named entries from `readers`.
- `allowNewParties` defaults to `false`. `frozen` defaults to `false`, but `/partyRosterFrozen=true` also freezes roster management at initialization. Approved admission additionally requires nonempty `admission/approvers`.
- `negotiation/allowedPaths` defaults to `[]`. A nonempty list enables negotiation over existing scalar fields. Paths must be distinct, contain no empty segments or `~`, and cannot target executable/control roots or configured access-document subtrees. Negotiation requires a document type and at least one required approver.
- `preActivationOperations`, `preActivationChannels` and `preActivationConnections` default to `[]`. They select exceptions to the acceptance gate, not to access or closure checks. Connection references select `clause` and `action` plus either `connection`, `automatic=true`, or `observations=true`. They require the standard connection planner. Direct timer and shared-channel references are rejected; workflow references do not themselves authorize an operation. Observation references select eligible sources only from actions marked `observation=true`. Retained references depend on the exact referenced clause remaining unchanged.
- `reviewedApprovals` defaults to `{}`. Each entry names a required party and supplies an `event` selector containing exactly `type`, `clause` and `subject`, plus non-root `source` and `basis` pointers. Optional `acceptanceBy` must name a different roster party. Duplicate selectors are rejected.

## Access and lifecycle

For each transport requiring Timeline Access, one matching executed access document must cover its exact timeline, match its provider and contain at least one key from every reader group. Different matching documents may cover different transports, but this check does not combine incomplete key coverage across documents for one transport. An empty reader group cannot satisfy it. Transports recognized as `External Channel` are exempt from this matching check; other supported transports must be `Timeline Channel` instances.

Installed access documents must retain the standard provider-controlled executable policy and contain initialization and provider-history evidence. Read permission does not confer operation authority. Permission changes remain provider-owned; emitting an access-update request does not grant access.

Initialization and embedded `Timeline Access Updated` deliveries refresh activation. These control deliveries remain admissible while business access is unavailable or the document is closed. `accessReady` and `functional` record access readiness, including current-revision pending additions. `termsAccepted` requires every `required` approval and equality between current negotiable fields and the agreed `terms/fields`. `active` additionally requires that `closed` is not true.

The maintained `status` distinguishes:

- `WAITING_FOR_ACCESS`: access is missing before first activation.
- `SUSPENDED_ACCESS`: access is missing after the document has previously activated.
- `AWAITING_ACCEPTANCE`: access is ready, but required acceptance or agreed-field consistency is missing.
- `ACTIVE`: access and acceptance are ready and the document is open.
- `CLOSED`: closure takes precedence over the other statuses.

`reason` is `PARTICIPANT_ACCESS_MISSING`, `ACCEPTANCE_REQUIRED`, or an empty string; it does not independently describe closure. `everActivated` preserves whether activation has occurred. First activation emits `Document Activated`; an active-to-access-deficit transition emits `Document Access Suspended`; renewed activation after an access deficit emits `Document Access Restored`.

The dispatch guard checks access before permitting configured pre-activation work. Other business deliveries require acceptance, current agreed fields and an open document. A denied delivery skips its handlers; external inputs are still consumed and checkpointed, so later activation does not replay them. Registered admission-consent operations have a separate exception only while their exact pending item, token, revision, channel and operation identities match.

## Acceptance and roster changes

`approve_<party>` requires the party’s lead channel, exact document-version review, the current activation `revision` and valid access. With negotiation enabled it also requires the current `termsRef`. A new approval emits `Terms Accepted`; repeating an existing approval has no additional acceptance effect. One party’s approval does not establish that the document is active.

For parties configured in `reviewedApprovals`, direct `approve`, `activate` and `proposeAndActivate` operations are blocked. The selected reviewed event must match the originating exact-review operation, actor, request, stored record and basis. An `approve` decision comes from the designated party. An `offer` records a scoped grant without accepting terms; an `accept` must come from `acceptanceBy` and match that grant’s document, party, revision, terms and proposal scope.

`updateParty_<party>` requires exact review, an unfrozen roster and a current party lead. Omitted input `party` selects the invoking party. Existing parties cannot manage another existing party; adding a new key requires `allowNewParties`. `replacement` requires a lead channel, valid representative names and sufficient access for the resulting roster. Success increments `revision`, clears approvals, adds a directly created party to `required`, and emits `Party Changed`.

Approved admission separately checks the expected revision, admission policy, main-party identity and access. It preserves the existing `required` list. `Party Addition Requested` installs supplied access histories and may emit transport-specific `Party Access Update Requested` events. Neither request is participant consent, an access grant or confirmation of admission. Pending access requirements can suspend progress before admission completes.

## Negotiated terms

`terms/ref` identifies the agreed definition and negotiable-field snapshot. `termsRevision` tracks changes to that identity separately from the activation `revision`. Changes to the roster or required approvers renew the terms identity, close a pending proposal as `AUTHORITY_CHANGED`, and clear approvals when negotiation is enabled.

Required approvers may use `proposeChanges`, `proposeAndActivate`, `activate`, `withdrawAcceptance`, `withdrawProposal` and `rejectProposal`, with exact document-version review. A proposal requires a unique `proposalId`, current `baseTermsRef` and nonempty `changes`, each with an allowed `path` and `replacement`. Duplicate paths, changed scalar kinds, invalid document candidates and unchanged terms are rejected. Replacing a pending proposal requires its identifier in `supersedes`; the old proposal becomes `SUPERSEDED`.

`activate` selects either current `termsRef` without `proposalId`, or proposed `termsRef` with its matching `proposalId`. Proposal acceptance remains separate from current-term approval until every required approver accepts. Completion applies the proposed fields, updates both revisions and the terms reference, records `APPLIED`, closes proposal editing and refreshes activation. `proposeAndActivate` combines proposing with the caller’s acceptance; it does not imply everyone has accepted.

Before first activation, required approvers may withdraw their own acceptance or reject the pending proposal; only its proposer may withdraw the proposal. These proposal outcomes are `REJECTED` and `WITHDRAWN`. First activation closes negotiation, including later acceptance withdrawal, and supersedes any remaining competing proposal. Direct clause changes are rejected in favor of party operations; while negotiation is configured and first activation has not occurred, changes to the clause set are also blocked.

Absent runtime state is unknown. Configuration defaults describe initialization behavior, not values to infer from missing state.
